title.en: Stopping by Woods on a Snowy Evening (Robert Frost)

text.en: Imagine stopping your cycle on a quiet road just to watch snow fall on a forest at night.

A traveller driving a horse-drawn sleigh pauses beside a forest on the darkest evening of the year to watch snow fall. The woods belong to someone who lives in the village and will not see him stop. His little horse finds the halt strange, because there is no farmhouse near, and shakes its harness bells as if to ask a question.
The woods are lovely, dark and deep, yet the speaker remembers his promises and the long road ahead. The repeated last line, miles to go before I sleep, can be read as duty to finish daily tasks and, for some readers, as the journey of life. The poem balances the pull of rest and beauty against responsibility.
Frost uses simple words, a regular rhyme pattern (each stanza's third line rhymes with the next stanza) and repetition for effect. Notice images such as downy flake, frozen lake and easy wind.
